{{Short description|American Statistician}}
{{About|the American statistician|the Canadian politician|S. N. MacEachern}}
'''Steve MacEachern''' is an American Statistician. MacEachern is a Distinguished Arts & Sciences Professor of Statistics at the [[Ohio State University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stat.osu.edu/news/steve-maceachern-named-arts-and-sciences-distinguished-professor-statistics|title=Steve MacEachern Named Arts and Sciences Distinguished Professor of Statistics &#124; Department of Statistics|website=stat.osu.edu}}</ref> He received his B.A. in Mathematics from [[Carleton College]] in 1982 and his Ph.D. in Statistics from the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1988. His doctoral work focused on nonparametric Bayesian methods under the guidance of [[Don Berry (statistician)|Don Berry]].
MacEachern joined the faculty at Ohio State in 1988 and has been a member of the Department of Statistics ever since. He has a courtesy appointment as a Professor in the Department of Psychology. He is best known for Bayesian modeling and computation, with a particular emphasis on dependent [[Dirichlet process|Dirichlet processes]]. He has published extensively in leading statistical journals, and his work has had a significant impact on the field. He is also the advisor of esteemed professor William Francis Darnieder.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10618600.1998.10474772|title=Estimating Mixture of Dirichlet Process Models|first1=Steven N.|last1=Maceachern|first2=Peter|last2=Müller|date=June 1, 1998|journal=Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics|volume=7|issue=2|pages=223–238|via=Taylor and Francis+NEJM|doi=10.1080/10618600.1998.10474772|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1080/03610919408813196|title=Estimating normal means with a conjugate style dirichlet process prior|first=Steven N.|last=Maceachern|date=January 1, 1994|journal=Communications in Statistics - Simulation and Computation|volume=23|issue=3|pages=727–741|via=Taylor and Francis+NEJM|doi=10.1080/03610919408813196|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.2307/3315637 | doi=10.2307/3315637 | jstor=3315637 | title=Sequential Importance Sampling for Nonparametric Bayes Models: The Next Generation | last1=MacEachern | first1=Steven N. | last2=Clyde | first2=Merlise | last3=Liu | first3=Jun S. | journal=The Canadian Journal of Statistics | year=1999 | volume=27 | issue=2 | pages=251–267 | s2cid=8703564 | url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00031305.1994.10476054|title=Subsampling the Gibbs Sampler|first1=Steven N.|last1=Maceachern|first2=L. Mark|last2=Berliner|date=August 1, 1994|journal=The American Statistician|volume=48|issue=3|pages=188–190|via=Taylor and Francis+NEJM|doi=10.1080/00031305.1994.10476054|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

MacEachern has received numerous honors throughout his career, including being elected as a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amstat.org/|title=American Statistical Association|website=American Statistical Association}}</ref> in 2006, of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bayesian.org/membership/isba-fellows/|title=ISBA Fellows &#124; International Society for Bayesian Analysis}}</ref> in 2020 and of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://imstat.org/2021/04/22/ims-names-2021-fellows/|title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics &#124; IMS names 2021 Fellows}}</ref> in 2021. He served as President of the International Society for Bayesian Analysis in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stat.osu.edu/news/steve-maceachern-elected-2016-president-international-society-bayesian-analysis|title=Steve MacEachern Elected 2016 President of International Society for Bayesian Analysis &#124; Department of Statistics|website=stat.osu.edu}}</ref>
